name: nh3h2o_evaporator_glide
title: Evaporator temperature glide of ammonia-water (Herold et al., Example 9.1)
summary: Three equilibrium states of an ammonia-water absorption system (Herold, Radermacher and Klein, Example 9.1): the desorber vapour in equilibrium with the rich solution (150 C, x = 0.3), the evaporator fed with saturated liquid of that composition at 0 C, and the saturated two-phase outlet with liquid mass fraction 0.25. Outputs: saturation pressures, vapour mass fractions, temperature glide (about 75 K) and outlet quality.
language_features: NH3H2O fluid (three of T, P, X, Q)

origin.notes: Example 9.1 of Herold, Radermacher and Klein, Absorption Chillers and Heat Pumps, CRC Press, 2nd ed., 2015; EES example of F-Chart Software, distributed by the EES-Community/ees-examples repository (commit 5c703d0, folder Case_Study/). The .eez companion stores the binary .EES with the solution used as verification reference. Credit: (c) F-Chart Software / S. A. Klein, MIT via EES-Community/ees-examples.

verification.summary: Solved in CoolSolve and compared with the EES stored solution (compare_solution.py --ees-units, 16 common variables): mass fractions y[1], y[2] agree within 0.02 %, y[3] 0.8 %, x_e2_min 3.4 %, temperatures/glide 0.9-3.1 %, Q[3] 1.1 %, pressures 1.9-4.3 % - the documented difference between the EES (Ibrahim-Klein) and CoolSolve (IAPWS G4-01) NH3H2O formulations.
verification.reference: EES stored solution of the binary Ex9_1.EES inside ex9_1.eez (ees_variables.csv), compared with tools/compare_solution.py --ees-units
verification.notes: max_rel_diff is the maximum over all 16 common variables (P[1], 4.34e-02). The 'only in EES' records (Q[1], Q[2], T[4..6], P[4..6], x[4..6]) are stale records of variables the equations do not define. The evaporator mass balance closes in both tools (hand-checked).

related_external: EES-Community/ees-examples Case_Study ex9_1 to ex9_5 (single-stage NH3H2O absorption family, Herold chapter 9)

history.action: added (native file solves in CoolSolve; compared with the EES stored solution)
